metadataRaw.title: How to Fix Sacroiliac Joint Pain FOR GOOD
metadataRaw.description:
Dr. Rowe demonstrates exercises that may help relieve sacroiliac (SI) joint pain for good.

If you’re unfamiliar with the sacroiliac joint (also called the SI joint), it’s a large joint in the pelvis that acts as a shock absorber for the spine above. When it becomes inflamed, it can cause a variety of issues, such as lower back pain that radiates across the buttocks and into the hips.

This pain is often caused by weakness and tightness that build up over time in the muscles supporting the SI joint—particularly the glutes (buttocks).

In this video, Dr. Rowe walks through exercises designed to both stretch and strengthen these muscles, providing quick and long-lasting relief from SI joint pain.

Each exercise works in a different way and will be shown in a variety of positions. For the best results, try them all and stick with the ones that bring you the most relief.

Watch now to learn how to fix sacroiliac joint pain at home—for good!

1:10 Seated Exercise
